features.method: Fluorescence-detector station position read from the triangle marker in Fig. 1 of arXiv:1410.3151 (layout of the Telescope Array: 507 square SDs, three triangles for the FD sites, a circle for the CLF). The figure is a to-scale map: the 505 station squares it shows (all but 1327 and 1428) register one-to-one onto the station table with a 0.27 pt rms (about 56 m), scale 4.78 pt/km east-west and 4.87 pt/km north-south; the triangle bounding-box centre is then read in the table frame (origin CLF, true east and north: see geometry:ta-sd-stations-strip-01) and converted with the same projection. The three bounding-box centres are 20.84, 20.83 and 20.84 km from the CLF, matching the papers' statement that the stations are equidistant from it, which supports taking the box centre rather than the triangle centroid (the centroid would shift each marker 0.3 km and break the equidistance). Accuracy 500 m: reading a marker from a plot, anchor of a triangle, and the frame (about 100 m). It is an outline-free point, not the building. This station: x = 17.037 km, y = -11.989 km from the CLF, 20.83 km away.

features.method: Convex hull of the 507 station positions of geometry:ta-sd-stations-strip-01 to -07 (17 vertices); a computed outline, not a published boundary. Frame: TASDPosition.dat (TA Collaboration data release on Zenodo, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.8405760, licence CC BY 4.0) lists 507 stations as x, y, z in km; the release states neither origin nor orientation. Both were established here by registering the table against a published map: Fig. 5 of arXiv:2103.01086 is a vector plot on latitude and longitude axes of the 507 TA SDs; its 507 red markers, read from the vector graphic and calibrated on the axis ticks, were matched one-to-one to the table and fitted to it. With the origin at the Central Laser Facility, 39.296918 N 112.908733 W (arXiv:1410.3151 section 5.1), x pointing east and y north, the fitted rotation is -0.001 deg and scale 1.0004, the CLF falls at table (0.006, 0.005) km, and the median residual is 14 m (90th percentile 26 m, 99th percentile 40 m) after a 6 m mean shift. A UTM zone 12 grid would be rotated by about 1.2 deg here, so the axes are true east and north. Stations are placed with an ellipsoidal azimuthal-equidistant projection about the CLF (WGS 84; agrees with a tangent-plane ENU to under 1 m at 25 km; a spherical equirectangular conversion would differ by up to 60 m at the array corners and fits the figure worse). The z column is not used. Each station is a 1.73 m square, the area-equivalent of one 3 m2 scintillator layer (arXiv:1201.4964: "Each layer of scintillator has an area of 3 m2"), so a position marker with the scintillator's area, not its outline. Accuracy 100 m covers the registration scatter, the origin (about 10 m) and the choice of projection.
